window-scare.summary: The 'second room' is the upstairs LANDING (house.js:30, `['landing', 4, 7, 7, 9, 'first', {wall:'wallpaper'}]` — world x[-4,4], z[0,6]), reached through the bedroom door (house.js:59); the wallpapered room with the big graveyard-facing window in Alex's screenshot is its south window at world (-1, F+1.8, 6). The scare is the scripted first WINDOW WATCHER in `buildWindowWatchers` (house.js:4236-4528), site index 0 (house.js:4241), which climbs the pane and then runs the SASH/FOLD/SKITTER entry that shoves it through the window into the room. It genuinely flashes: the only interval in which the figure is fully framed above the sill with its palm on the glass is the 0.85 s `sash` phase (house.js:4397), and the in-room payoff is 0.55 s of folding plus 0.4167 s of visible fade (house.js:4410, 4424, 4434) — under one second each. Worse, three separate paths consume the scripted event permanently and instantly on first contact: stepping within 2.1 m of the window (house.js:4481), looking away for 0.55 s once it has been seen (house.js:4505, whose scripted guard at 4509 is dead code because the event spawns at exactly `w.t = 0.5`), and the unwatched creep at `dt/6` (house.js:4501) which self-completes the whole beat in 3 s whether or not the player ever faced it. Staring at it actually makes it leave sooner (`dt/3.1`, house.js:4489), it has no line-of-sight test (unlike `_isObserved`, enemies.js:2619), and its only audio cue fires on the same frame it becomes visible (house.js:4465-4467), inverting the audio-first law.

window-scare.diagnosis:
It is not one bug; it is five, and they compound.

1. THE DWELL IS GENUINELY SHORT. The figure is only fully framed above the sill — torso, palm and fingers in the glass — once `w.t` reaches 1. The very next tick fires the entry (house.js:4518), so the fully-risen pose exists for exactly the 0.85 s `sash` phase (house.js:4397). Everything before that is a head-sliver cresting a 1.0 m sill; everything after is descent. Total legible time at the pane: 0.85 s. That alone matches Alex's 'less than a second'.

2. THE PAYOFF IS FADED OUT IN 0.42 s AND HALF-BURIED IN THE FLOOR. `fold` runs 0.55 s (house.js:4410) to `entry.to.y = s.floor - 1.05` (house.js:4401) — the root origin one metre BELOW the landing floorboards, which puts the torso (local y 1.0) inside the floor and leaves only head/shoulders at F+0.55. Then `skitter` fades `w.fade -= dt * 2.4` (house.js:4424), so `root.visible` goes false after 0.4167 s even though the phase runs 1.45 s (house.js:4434). The 'it is in the room with you' moment is under a second of half-clipped geometry.

3. LOOKING AT IT MAKES IT LEAVE SOONER. Watched advance is `dt/3.1` (house.js:4489) vs the unwatched creep `dt/6` (house.js:4501). The same scalar that drives the climb also triggers the exit, so a player who does the right thing — turns and stares — burns the beat down in 1.55 s instead of 3.0 s. This is exactly backwards from the crawler, whose progress advances only while watched (house.js:4828) precisely so the player controls the pace.

4. THREE INSTANT, PERMANENT KILL SWITCHES, ALL ARMED FROM FRAME ONE. (a) `if (planar < 2.1 && w.t > 0.05) vanish('close')` (house.js:4481) — the scripted event spawns at `w.t = 0.5` (house.js:4463), so the proximity trip is live immediately; walking up to the big graveyard window (the single most natural reaction, and the exact vantage in Alex's screenshot) deletes it in one frame with a whisper. (b) `lookAwayT > 0.55` -> `vanish('away')` (house.js:4505-4510); the author's own belt-and-braces guard `if (scripted && w.t < 0.5)` (house.js:4509) is DEAD CODE — spawn sets w.t to exactly 0.5 and the comparison is strict `<`, so it never protects anything. Glance, glance away for half a second, gone forever. (c) Every vanish does `w.seen++` (house.js:4375), and `scripted` is `w.seen === 0 && w.siteIndex === 0` (house.js:4472), so there is no second chance — subsequent hauntings are the generic climb-and-vanish, which never enters the window at all.

5. IT IS GATED TO FIRE WHEN NOBODY IS LOOKING, AND IT COMPLETES ITSELF UNSEEN. `w.cooldown = 6` (house.js:4343) starts the moment the player crosses x<4 out of the bedroom zone (house.js:769-771). At WALK = 2.7 m/s (player.js:10) the player is 16 m of travel later — the landing's traffic runs along z~1 from the bedroom door at (4,1) to the nursery door at (-4,1) or the stair door at (1,0), i.e. westward/northward, with the window 5 m BEHIND at (-1,6) on a bearing ~39 deg off the walk direction, outside the `dot > 0.93` (~21.6 deg) cone (house.js:4479). Many players are already in the nursery at T+6. And because the unwatched creep (house.js:4501) completes in 3 s regardless, the whole sash/fold/skitter runs off-camera and `finishEntry` sets both flags (house.js:4369-4370). Proof: `windowWatcherSeen` and `windowWatcherEntered` show up in flag dumps of eight completely unrelated relay/void-door scenarios in tests/results/house-expansion.json (lines 211-212, 289-290, 476-477, 531-532, 586-587, 641-642, 815-816, 921-922) — nothing in those tests ever looked at the landing window.

6. AUDIO-FIRST IS INVERTED. `glassTink` fires on the same frame as `root.visible = true` (house.js:4465-4467) — a 0.3 s decay chime from up to 8.5 m away, simultaneous with the reveal, not before it. The long, legible `sashScrape` (audio.js:933, 0.72 s sweep with judder) arrives only at the entry trigger (house.js:4524), i.e. after the figure has finished climbing. You never hear it before you see it.

7. NO OCCLUSION TEST. `watched` (house.js:4478-4479) is pure distance + dot with no line-of-sight, unlike `_isObserved` (enemies.js:2619-2637). A player in the nursery facing the shared partition counts as 'watching', which advances the fast climb, sets `everWatched = true`, and then arms the 0.55 s look-away kill — all while the figure is behind a wall. Not culling; the opposite — it is being consumed through geometry.

edit_points.title: Audio lead-in BEFORE any pixels (audio-first law)
edit_points.change: Introduce `const LEAD_IN = 1.4;` and a new `w.phase = 'listen'`. On arm: keep `w.t = 0.5` and position the rig, but leave `root.visible = false`; play `game.audio.sashScrape({ pos: paneCenter, gain: 0.45, rate: 1.25, verb: 0.6 })` (a scrape on the OUTSIDE of the sill) instead of the glassTink, then a `game.audio.creak` at LEAD_IN*0.5, and only reveal (`root.visible = true` + the existing `glassTink`) once `w.leadT >= LEAD_IN`. Model: the crawler will not become visible until `gazeT >= 0.32` and whispers at the moment of trigger (house.js:4819-4827). Constant to add: LEAD_IN = 1.4 s. Constant to move: the `glassTink({gain:0.5, rate:0.5})` on house.js:4467.

edit_points.title: Cap the unwatched creep so the beat can never be consumed off-camera
edit_points.change: Change to `w.t = Math.min(0.82, w.t + dt / 5)`. The figure still creeps up to a clearly-visible three-quarters pose unattended (so a head turned by the lead-in catches it mid-climb), but only WATCHED time (house.js:4489) can carry it the last 18% to 1.0. This makes the beat impossible to complete unseen, which is what the recorded flag dumps in tests/results/house-expansion.json prove is currently happening. Keep the existing act-change/death hard-finish at house.js:4392/4438 as the safety valve.

edit_points.title: Stop punishing the player for staring; make watching HOLD it, not hurry it
edit_points.change: Slow to `dt / 4.5` (matching the crawler's `dt / 4.15`, house.js:4828) so the climb from 0.5 reads as ~2.3 s of watched rise rather than 1.55 s. Pair with edit 4 so the total on-screen time goes UP when the player engages. Branch the rate on `scripted` if the four generic haunting sites should stay quick.

edit_points.title: Add a HOLD-AT-PANE state — the multi-second scare Alex is asking for
edit_points.change: Insert a new `entry.state = 'press'` before `'sash'`. Add `const HOLD_AT_PANE = 3.0;`. During `press`: root stays at the fully-risen pose, `head.rotation` tracks the player by a small clamped yaw, a `glassTink({gain:0.5, rate:0.38})` fires as the palm settles, and `palm.position.z` eases 0.02 m further into the glass (a lean, not a pop). Only after `entry.t >= HOLD_AT_PANE` AND the view-cone proof of edit 5 is satisfied does it advance to `'sash'`. Add `'press'` to the state list at house.js:4387 so the entry branch owns the ticker. This alone converts the beat's legible dwell from 0.85 s to ~3.9 s.

edit_points.title: Only retreat/enter after it has PROVABLY been in the player's view cone
edit_points.anchor: house.js:4478-4479 (`watched`) and the new gate in edit 4
edit_points.change: Add `w.viewT = 0;` to the state object (house.js:4343) and accumulate `w.viewT += dt` only when `watched && losClear`. For `losClear`, follow the proven pattern in `_isObserved` (enemies.js:2619-2637): a throttled structural segment test refreshed every 0.08 s so a wall between the player and the pane does not count as watching. If you do not want to reach into enemies.js, reuse the local occluder-aware helper `isWatched(point, minDot = 0.91, maxDistance = 8.5)` at house.js:5013-5021 — it already carries the `Math.abs(eye.y - point.y) > 2.15` floor/ceiling reject — and add one `_segmentBlocked`-equivalent call. Gate: `const WATCH_PROOF = 2.0;` — the entry may not advance past `press` until `w.viewT >= WATCH_PROOF`. Also loosen the cone from `> 0.93` to `> 0.88` (~28 deg) so a player crossing the landing peripherally accrues proof. The cone change and the LOS gate must ship TOGETHER.

edit_points.title: Replace the look-away DELETE with the crawler's look-away FREEZE
edit_points.change: For `scripted`, never call `vanish('away')`. Mirror house.js:4885-4903: while unwatched, simply stop advancing `w.t` (freeze the climb, leave it visible) — the exact behaviour pinned for the crawler by tests/house-critical-path-regression.mjs:878 ('looking away freezes its physical progress'). Delete the dead guard at house.js:4509 (`if (scripted && w.t < 0.5)` can never be true given `w.t = 0.5` at house.js:4463) and replace it with `if (scripted) { w.lookAwayT = 0; return; }`. Generic later hauntings (`!scripted`) keep the existing 0.55 s vanish grammar untouched.

edit_points.title: Stop the close-approach from deleting the scripted beat
edit_points.change: Exempt the scripted event: `if (!scripted && planar < 2.1 && w.t > 0.05) { vanish('close'); return; }`. Walking up to the window is the correct player response and must not cancel the payoff. Then, to keep the collider-free body out of the player capsule during `fold`/`skitter`, adopt the crawler's answer: a `proximityThreshold` (house.js:4746, 1.48 m) that triggers a visible recoil over ~0.48 s (house.js:4926) rather than an instant hide — i.e. the thing shrinks back toward the sash instead of blinking out.

edit_points.title: Slow the entry itself so the crossing is watchable
edit_points.change: sash: `smoothstep(0, 0.7, entry.t)` -> `smoothstep(0, 1.5, entry.t)` and the exit gate `entry.t >= 0.85` -> `entry.t >= 1.7`. fold: `smoothstep(0, 0.55, entry.t)` -> `smoothstep(0, 1.1, entry.t)` and `entry.t >= 0.55` -> `entry.t >= 1.1`. skitter: fade `w.fade - dt * 2.4` -> `w.fade - dt * 0.6` (1.67 s of visible retreat) and `entry.t >= 1.45` -> `entry.t >= 2.6`. Re-space `ENTRY_SCUFFS` (house.js:4330-4335) across the longer skitter: at 0.25 / 0.8 / 1.4 / 2.05. Net legible time from first sight to gone: ~9 s instead of ~1.8 s.

edit_points.title: Fix the in-room landing pose (currently half-sunk in the floorboards)
edit_points.change: `s.floor - 1.05` puts the root origin a metre below the landing floor, so the torso (local y 1.0, house.js:4268) is inside the boards and only the head clears at F+0.55. Use `s.floor - 0.30` and carry the crouch with `root.scale.y` instead, so head and shoulders sit at a legible crouch height. This is exactly the fix the crawler already documents at house.js:4852-4856 ('this weight shift leaves the head and shoulders visibly in-room').

edit_points.title: Arm it when the player is actually IN the landing
edit_points.anchor: house.js:4343 (`cooldown: 6`) and the arm block at house.js:4444-4468
edit_points.change: 6 s after the bedroom threshold routinely lands the player in the nursery or at the stair door. Gate the scripted arm on presence instead of a bare timer: require `game.act === 'house' && Math.abs(game.player.pos.y - F) < 1.5 && p.x > -4 && p.x < 4 && p.z > 0 && p.z < 6` (the landing's world bounds derived from house.js:30) plus a short settle, and raise the fallback `cooldown` to 9. Precedent: the crawler's `inScullery` box test at house.js:4798-4799.

risks: Capping the unwatched creep (edit 2) means a player who never enters or never looks at the landing leaves the beat un-consumed. The act-change/death hard-finish at house.js:4392 and 4438 MUST stay so `windowWatcherEntered` and the permanently-cracked sash still land — several unrelated scenarios already record those flags (tests/results/house-expansion.json:211-212, 815-816) and the sash-open world state is described as 'forever' at house.js:4356.

Stretching the beat to ~9 s pushes it toward HOUSE_RESIDENT_DELAY = 18 (director.js:30). Combined with edit 10's presence gate (which delays arming until the player is in the landing), a slow player could have the watcher entering the window while the Resident is spawning. Check the overlap before shipping.

`root.visible` is currently written from five places (house.js:4426, 4457, 4465, 4490, 4521). Adding a `'press'` state and a lead-in invisible phase without auditing all five will produce exactly the one-frame pop the fix is meant to remove.

Adding a line-of-sight test (edit 5) either couples house.js to `Enemies._isObserved`/`_segmentBlocked` (enemies.js:2619-2637, private methods) or duplicates the ray. Prefer extracting the existing local `isWatched` at house.js:5013 into a shared helper rather than a third copy of the same dot-product.

Exempting the scripted event from the 2.1 m proximity vanish (edit 7) means a player can stand inside the fold/skitter path. The rig has no collider, so without the recoil replacement the figure will visibly pass through the player's head — the exact failure the crawler's 1.48 m tripwire (house.js:4746, 4913-4917) exists to prevent.

`sashPane` is adopted by a fragile scene.traverse that matches PlaneGeometry + color 0x0a1016 within 0.45 m (house.js:4304-4313). If the world's glass recipe drifts, sashPane is null and only `sashRail` moves. A slower, longer sash animation (edit 8) makes that silent failure far more visible on screen.

Slowing the watched climb rate (edit 3) also affects the four NON-scripted haunting sites (nursery, dining, kitchen, guest — house.js:4242-4245), which share the same `dt / 3.1` line. If you want the generic hauntings to stay quick, branch the rate on `scripted`.
Widening the cone from 0.93 to 0.88 (edit 5) with no LOS test would make the through-the-wall false-positive WORSE. Edit 5's cone change and its LOS gate must ship together, not separately.
tests: NOTHING PINS THIS BEAT. It passes within a couple of metres of the window and asserts nothing about the watcher — a ready insertion point for a 'the second room's window scare was on screen for >= N seconds' beat.

Pursuit is a two-rail fairness model: chases heardPos breadcrumbs (never live coords) at lerp(drySpeed 1.55, heardSpeed 4.35, heardStrength); a walker sustains heardStrength ~0.68 => 3.45 m/s vs WALK 2.7 (closing 0.75 m/s); a runner outruns 4.35 < RUN 4.7. First catch nonfatal (e.warned); caveSpray RE-ARMS the grace (enemies.js:1102) — four authored curtains are effectively four extra lives. Spray cuts speed to 0.35x for up to ~2.6 s AND vetoes new commits while wetT > 0. The spec pushes the spawn far ahead ALONG THE ROUTE (new arc-length helpers; projectUnderfalls returns routeDistance NULL inside the chapel disc — do not use it), raises drySpeed only (heardSpeed untouched — the run-escape rail), shortens the commit, opens the sluice dy gate, weakens/shortens the spray slow — every number checked against the two inequalities that keep a WALKING bot alive. At k=0 (the raised beat Alex screenshotted) the rotation is the captured `lowered` pose (rx -0.06, ry ±0.34, rz ±0.05): worked through the rig's axes (+Z fingers, +Y dorsum), the fingers point AT the camera and the dorsum faces the ceiling — two flat hands, palms down, fingertips aimed at your face.
